system_prompt:
You are an eighth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Of the 400 students in a school, 50 plan to go to university, 100 to a polytechnic school, 150 to a business college, and the remainder plan to enter workforce.

Use the circle below to make a pie chart showing the proportions of students planning to do each of these. Put labels on your chart.

[Image: A circle with a point in the middle and 8 equally spaced points placed around the circumference of the circle.]

Figure, described in words:
A circle with a central point and 8 equally spaced dots along its circumference, corresponding to the 12:00, 1:30, 3:00, 4:30, 6:00, 7:30, 9:00, and 10:30 clock positions.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Counts: university 50 (1/8 of 400), polytechnic 100 (1/4), business college 150 (3/8), workforce 400 - 50 - 100 - 150 = 100 (1/4). Angles: university 50/400 x 360 = 45 degrees; polytechnic 100/400 x 360 = 90 degrees; business college 150/400 x 360 = 135 degrees; workforce 100/400 x 360 = 90 degrees (total 360). On the circle, using the 8 equally spaced points (each 45 degrees apart), draw: from the 12:00 point to the 1:30 point, one radius pair forming a 45-degree sector labeled 'University (50 students, 1/8)'; from the 1:30 point to the 3:00 point, plus the next 45-degree step, i.e. from 1:30 to 4:30, a 90-degree sector labeled 'Polytechnic (100 students, 1/4)'; from 4:30 to 9:00 (going clockwise through 6:00 and 7:30), a 135-degree sector labeled 'Business college (150 students, 3/8)'; from 9:00 back to 12:00 (through 10:30), a 90-degree sector labeled 'Workforce (100 students, 1/4)'. Draw radii from the center to each of the separating points so the four sectors meet at the center, shade or color each sector differently, and add a key or label each sector with its category and number of students.
